# Changelog

All notable changes to carrier-utils.

## Unreleased

- Fix `map_edi_210_charges` treating zero-dollar EDI 210 lines as real charges:
  the ignore check covered only one-cent lines, so a zero-amount `DET` detention
  line was categorized as detention from its code and added invoice-review noise.
  Zero-dollar lines now return category `ignore` with amount `0.00` and source
  `amount`, while non-zero lines (including non-zero `DET`) keep their existing
  categorization and source (CT-235).
- Fix `calculate_team_driver_premium` subtracting a contract's flat addition
  instead of adding it: the flat add-on is now applied on top of the
  multiplier-adjusted premium, so a 300-mile team request under a 1.10x contract
  with a $20.00 flat addition returns $79.40 instead of $39.40. Contracts with
  no flat addition price unchanged (CT-234).
- Fix `allocate_toll_costs` raising a validation error on zero-toll and zero-mile
  segments: zero values are now treated as non-billable and skipped rather than
  rejected (negative values are still invalid), so a trip with a waived $5.00 toll
  over 12 miles, a $0.00 toll over 12 miles and an $8.00 toll over 0.00 miles
  allocates $0.00 to customer, driver and carrier instead of failing before
  settlement. Shipments with only billable segments allocate unchanged (CT-232).
- Fix `find_excursions` carrying a reefer excursion across a logger gap: the
  logger-gap split compared each reading against itself instead of the previous
  reading, so a gap never ended the run and the excursion looked closed and
  longer than observed. An out-of-range run now ends at the last reading before
  a gap longer than 15 minutes and is reported as open, so the reported case
  (readings every 5 minutes 22:00-22:30, then nothing until 23:10 at 34F) is a
  30.0-minute open excursion ending 22:30 instead of a closed 70.0-minute one.
  Excursions over continuous readings are unchanged (CT-233).
- Fix `calculate_mode_conversion_factor` applying the hazmat uplift to drayage
  conversions as a subtraction instead of an addition: a hazmat truckload-to-drayage
  move of 12,000 lb over 200 miles with 2 stops now returns 0.7700 (0.7600 base plus
  the 0.0100 drayage hazmat uplift) instead of 0.7500, correcting every hazmat
  drayage quote and settlement tied to this factor. Non-hazmat conversions and
  hazmat conversions to other target modes are unchanged (CT-231).
- Fix `calculate_washout_fee` applying the hazmat washout premium even when the
  contract disallows it: the pass-through maximum is now the standard rate when
  `allow_hazmat_premium` is false, so a hazmat load with a $220.00 receipt
  reimburses $70.00 instead of $205.00. Contracts that allow the premium keep
  the full hazmat maximum and settle unchanged (CT-230).

- Fix `calculate_driver_medical_due` keeping drivers in grace past the documented
  15-day post-expiration window: `GRACE_DAYS` is now 15 instead of 16, so a record
  that expired 16 days ago returns status `expired` with no grace end date, and a
  record that expired 3 days ago returns a grace end date of 2026-04-13 instead of
  2026-04-14. Records still within grace keep returning `grace` and remain
  dispatch-ineligible (CT-228).
- Fix `parse_rate_confirmation` reading trailing note numbers as the amount: a
  dollar amount now wins over numbers in a note that follows it, so Hartline
  multi-stop rate con TW-88412 parses `Stop Off: $100.00 (1 extra stop)` as
  $100.00 (not $1.00) and `Detention: $75.00/hr after 2 hrs free` as $75.00 (not
  $2.00), letting the flat charges tie out to the $2,847.50 total. Rate cons
  without trailing notes parse unchanged (CT-229).

- Fix `calculate_short_pay_variance` understating the early-pay discount by
  subtracting fuel from the discount base instead of adding it: the discount is
  now a percent of the full pre-tax subtotal (linehaul + fuel + accessorial +
  other, tax excluded), so an invoice of $1,155.00 (linehaul $1,000.00, fuel
  $100.00, tax $55.00) with a $1,133.00 payment on the due date shows an
  expected amount of $1,133.00 and no short pay instead of a $4.00 short pay
  (CT-225).

- Fix `calculate_trailer_inspection_due` marking hazmat trailers due a day early:
  the hazmat calendar limit is now the documented 45 days instead of 44, so a
  California hazmat trailer last inspected on day 0 at 40,000 miles and read on
  day 44 at 47,000 miles is due February 15, 2026 with reason `hazmat` rather
  than February 14, 2026. Non-hazmat and other-jurisdiction schedules are
  unchanged (CT-226).
- Fix `calculate_breakdown_pay` overpaying overnight breakdown stipends by one cent:
  the stipend is $85.00 per midnight crossed (was $85.01), so a breakdown reported at
  22:00 on 2026-04-02 and repaired at 03:00 on 2026-04-03 now pays $139.00 instead of
  $139.01. Same-day breakdown pay is unchanged (CT-227).
- Fix `calculate_inside_delivery_fee` omitting the threshold heavy-handling bump at
  exactly 25 pieces: the bump was only applied above 25 pieces, so a threshold stop
  with 1 floor, no elevator and 25 pieces priced at $115.00 instead of $125.50.
  Threshold stops now get the bump at 25 or more pieces as documented, while
  non-threshold services and counts below 25 keep their current pricing (CT-223).
- Fix `build_invoice` reporting a subtotal that does not tie out to the printed
  lines: the subtotal is now the sum of the rounded line amounts instead of a
  re-rounding of the unrounded extended charges, so INV-204417 prints lines of
  $2,989.27, $545.82 and $125.03 with a subtotal and total of $3,660.12 rather
  than $3,660.11. Invoices whose line rounding already tied out are unchanged
  (CT-222).
- Fix `calculate_trailer_inspection_due` raising `TypeError` for a failed last
  inspection: the reinspection reason suffix was built with string subtraction
  instead of concatenation, so failed-inspection trailers got no due date or
  odometer limit at all. A trailer inspected at 70,000 miles, now at 70,499
  miles on day 6 with a failed result now returns day 7 / 70,500 miles with
  reason `standard+reinspect` (CT-220).
- Fix `find_excursions` dropping a 30-minute reefer excursion whose first
  in-range reading is also the reading that closes it: the excursion now ends at
  the first reading back inside the range (as documented) rather than the last
  out-of-range reading, so TW-91033 (setpoint 34F +/- 4, 39F or warmer 22:05
  through 22:30, 37F at 22:35) is reported as a 30-minute excursion instead of
  nothing (CT-221).
- Fix `find_conflicts` in `dock_schedule` missing overlaps behind a long unload:
  each appointment is now checked against every earlier appointment still holding
  the door, not just the immediate predecessor, so a floor-load unload booked
  08:00-12:00 reports conflicts with later appointments at 09:00 and 10:00
  instead of only the first one (CT-219).
- Fix `calculate_edi_997_ack_status` accepting a materially incomplete 997
  interchange: the overage rate was forced to zero whenever included transactions
  exceeded accepted plus rejected, so any shortfall passed tolerance. A 997 with
  9,950 accepted of 10,000 included (0.50% overage, matching control numbers) now
  returns `COUNT_MISMATCH` under the 0.20% default overage tolerance, while
  within-tolerance overage and exact counts still return `ACCEPTED` (CT-218).
- Fix `parse_bol_references` lifting an all-zero payload to `1`: a reference such
  as `PU-0` now stays `ParsedReference("PU", "0")` instead of becoming
  `ParsedReference("PU", "1")`, so valid pickup numbers are no longer shifted to
  a different identifier (CT-216).

- Fix `fuel_surcharge_for_shipment` billing Fri-Sun pickups at the following
  Monday's DOE price: the surcharge now uses the most recent price published on
  or before the pickup date, so TW-90266 (Friday 2026-09-18, 1,000 mi) bills
  $470.00 at the 9/14 price of $4.03 instead of $430.00 at 9/21's $3.79 (CT-217).
- Fix `map_edi_210_charges` mapping unknown nonblank EDI 210 charge codes to
  `misc` instead of the generic `other` bucket: an unknown code such as `ABC`
  now maps to `other` with source `fallback`. Blank codes still use the
  amount-threshold fallback, and `999` keeps its existing `other` mapping
  (CT-215).
- Fix `calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement` overcounting remaining quarterly
  selections: the year is now treated as four quarters instead of three, so a
  40-driver pool at a 25% annual rate with 4 prior selections returns 3 for the
  current quarter rather than 6 (CT-213).
- Fix `calculate_mode_conversion_factor` inflating LTL-to-truckload conversions by
  a basis point: the LTL-to-truckload base factor is corrected to 0.8500 (was
  0.8501), so a 10,000 lb move over 1,000 miles with 2 stops now returns 0.8200
  instead of 0.8201 (CT-214).

- Fix `calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement` rejecting `period_number` 12 for
  monthly programs: December is now a valid final period, so the requirement is
  calculated (and capped at the eligible population) instead of raising
  `ValueError` (CT-212).
- Fix `allocate_fuel_purchases` raising on eligible zero-mile trips: a
  zero-odometer-change trip is now valid and the purchase is allocated to the
  first eligible trip instead of failing before settlement (CT-211).

- Fix `tender_expires_at` expiring Friday-evening tenders on Saturday 09:00
  instead of the next business morning: the next-business-day rollover no
  longer stops on Saturday (or skips to Tuesday from a weekend), so a Friday
  18:00 tender now expires Monday 09:00 (CT-210).
- Fix `lookup_lane_rate` falling straight to the customer default when the most
  specific lane rate on file has expired: an expired lane now falls back to the
  next less specific level (for example Hartline's OR to ID state rate) instead
  of the default per-mile rate (CT-209).
- Fix `ifta_return` dropping jurisdictions with tax-paid fuel but no miles
  driven: a fuel-only member jurisdiction now gets a line with zero taxable
  gallons so its tax-paid gallons come back as a credit (CT-208).
- Fix `calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement` rejecting a valid zero annual
  rate: `annual_rate=0` now returns zero selections instead of raising
  `ValueError`, while negative rates are still rejected (CT-206).
- Fix false 30-minute break violations in `break_violations`: consecutive
  non-driving segments (for example an on-duty fuel stop followed by an
  off-duty meal) now add up toward the break (CT-205).
- Fix `estimate_arrival` producing ETAs that are too early for drivers who
  spent on-duty time loading before departure: the 30-minute break now counts
  against the remaining 14-hour window, so a run that cannot finish in the
  window schedules the required 10-hour reset (CT-204).
- Fix `check_axle_weights` missing bridge-formula violations on interior axle
  groups: every group of two or more consecutive axles is now checked, not just
  the outer bridge (CT-203).
- Fix long-haul discount being added instead of subtracted at 1,000+ paid miles
  in `calculate_linehaul_rate_per_mile` (CT-202).
- Fix multi-line LTL quotes overstating linear feet: lines with the same pallet
  footprint now share rows in `linear_feet_for_shipment`.

from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from inside_delivery_fee import (
    InsideDeliveryRequest,
    InsideDeliveryTerms,
    calculate_inside_delivery_fee,
)


def test_room_of_choice_uses_base_when_above_minimum():
    request = InsideDeliveryRequest(
        service_level="room_of_choice",
        floor_count=1,
        has_elevator=False,
        piece_count=4,
    )
    assert calculate_inside_delivery_fee(request) == Decimal("85.00")


def test_one_floor_is_included_and_ground_floor_has_no_surcharge():
    floor_one = InsideDeliveryRequest("room_of_choice", 1, False, 1)
    ground = InsideDeliveryRequest("room_of_choice", 0, False, 1)
    assert calculate_inside_delivery_fee(floor_one) == Decimal("85.00")
    assert calculate_inside_delivery_fee(ground) == Decimal("85.00")


def test_extra_floors_without_elevator_bill_full_rate():
    request = InsideDeliveryRequest(
        service_level="room_of_choice",
        floor_count=3,
        has_elevator=False,
        piece_count=2,
    )
    assert calculate_inside_delivery_fee(request) == Decimal("135.00")


def test_extra_floors_with_elevator_bill_reduced_rate():
    request = InsideDeliveryRequest(
        service_level="room_of_choice",
        floor_count=3,
        has_elevator=True,
        piece_count=2,
    )
    assert calculate_inside_delivery_fee(request) == Decimal("113.00")


def test_white_glove_includes_more_pieces_before_surcharge():
    request = InsideDeliveryRequest(
        service_level="white_glove",
        floor_count=2,
        has_elevator=True,
        piece_count=18,
    )
    assert calculate_inside_delivery_fee(request) == Decimal("170.50")


def test_threshold_with_25_pieces_includes_heavy_handling_bump():
    request = InsideDeliveryRequest(
        service_level="threshold",
        floor_count=1,
        has_elevator=False,
        piece_count=25,
    )
    assert calculate_inside_delivery_fee(request) == Decimal("125.50")


def test_threshold_below_25_pieces_does_not_include_heavy_handling_bump():
    request = InsideDeliveryRequest(
        service_level="threshold",
        floor_count=1,
        has_elevator=False,
        piece_count=24,
    )
    assert calculate_inside_delivery_fee(request) == Decimal("111.50")


def test_non_threshold_services_do_not_receive_threshold_heavy_handling_bump():
    request = InsideDeliveryRequest(
        service_level="room_of_choice",
        floor_count=1,
        has_elevator=False,
        piece_count=25,
    )
    assert calculate_inside_delivery_fee(request) == Decimal("137.50")


def test_custom_minimum_can_raise_otherwise_computed_amount():
    request = InsideDeliveryRequest(
        service_level="room_of_choice",
        floor_count=1,
        has_elevator=False,
        piece_count=1,
    )
    terms = InsideDeliveryTerms(minimum_charge=Decimal("95.00"))
    assert calculate_inside_delivery_fee(request, terms) == Decimal("95.00")

# Changelog

All notable changes to carrier-utils.

## Unreleased

- Fix `map_edi_210_charges` treating zero-dollar EDI 210 lines as real charges:
  the ignore check covered only one-cent lines, so a zero-amount `DET` detention
  line was categorized as detention from its code and added invoice-review noise.
  Zero-dollar lines now return category `ignore` with amount `0.00` and source
  `amount`, while non-zero lines (including non-zero `DET`) keep their existing
  categorization and source (CT-235).
- Fix `calculate_team_driver_premium` subtracting a contract's flat addition
  instead of adding it: the flat add-on is now applied on top of the
  multiplier-adjusted premium, so a 300-mile team request under a 1.10x contract
  with a $20.00 flat addition returns $79.40 instead of $39.40. Contracts with
  no flat addition price unchanged (CT-234).
- Fix `allocate_toll_costs` raising a validation error on zero-toll and zero-mile
  segments: zero values are now treated as non-billable and skipped rather than
  rejected (negative values are still invalid), so a trip with a waived $5.00 toll
  over 12 miles, a $0.00 toll over 12 miles and an $8.00 toll over 0.00 miles
  allocates $0.00 to customer, driver and carrier instead of failing before
  settlement. Shipments with only billable segments allocate unchanged (CT-232).
- Fix `find_excursions` carrying a reefer excursion across a logger gap: the
  logger-gap split compared each reading against itself instead of the previous
  reading, so a gap never ended the run and the excursion looked closed and
  longer than observed. An out-of-range run now ends at the last reading before
  a gap longer than 15 minutes and is reported as open, so the reported case
  (readings every 5 minutes 22:00-22:30, then nothing until 23:10 at 34F) is a
  30.0-minute open excursion ending 22:30 instead of a closed 70.0-minute one.
  Excursions over continuous readings are unchanged (CT-233).
- Fix `calculate_mode_conversion_factor` applying the hazmat uplift to drayage
  conversions as a subtraction instead of an addition: a hazmat truckload-to-drayage
  move of 12,000 lb over 200 miles with 2 stops now returns 0.7700 (0.7600 base plus
  the 0.0100 drayage hazmat uplift) instead of 0.7500, correcting every hazmat
  drayage quote and settlement tied to this factor. Non-hazmat conversions and
  hazmat conversions to other target modes are unchanged (CT-231).
- Fix `calculate_washout_fee` applying the hazmat washout premium even when the
  contract disallows it: the pass-through maximum is now the standard rate when
  `allow_hazmat_premium` is false, so a hazmat load with a $220.00 receipt
  reimburses $70.00 instead of $205.00. Contracts that allow the premium keep
  the full hazmat maximum and settle unchanged (CT-230).

- Fix `calculate_driver_medical_due` keeping drivers in grace past the documented
  15-day post-expiration window: `GRACE_DAYS` is now 15 instead of 16, so a record
  that expired 16 days ago returns status `expired` with no grace end date, and a
  record that expired 3 days ago returns a grace end date of 2026-04-13 instead of
  2026-04-14. Records still within grace keep returning `grace` and remain
  dispatch-ineligible (CT-228).
- Fix `parse_rate_confirmation` reading trailing note numbers as the amount: a
  dollar amount now wins over numbers in a note that follows it, so Hartline
  multi-stop rate con TW-88412 parses `Stop Off: $100.00 (1 extra stop)` as
  $100.00 (not $1.00) and `Detention: $75.00/hr after 2 hrs free` as $75.00 (not
  $2.00), letting the flat charges tie out to the $2,847.50 total. Rate cons
  without trailing notes parse unchanged (CT-229).

- Fix `calculate_short_pay_variance` understating the early-pay discount by
  subtracting fuel from the discount base instead of adding it: the discount is
  now a percent of the full pre-tax subtotal (linehaul + fuel + accessorial +
  other, tax excluded), so an invoice of $1,155.00 (linehaul $1,000.00, fuel
  $100.00, tax $55.00) with a $1,133.00 payment on the due date shows an
  expected amount of $1,133.00 and no short pay instead of a $4.00 short pay
  (CT-225).

- Fix `calculate_trailer_inspection_due` marking hazmat trailers due a day early:
  the hazmat calendar limit is now the documented 45 days instead of 44, so a
  California hazmat trailer last inspected on day 0 at 40,000 miles and read on
  day 44 at 47,000 miles is due February 15, 2026 with reason `hazmat` rather
  than February 14, 2026. Non-hazmat and other-jurisdiction schedules are
  unchanged (CT-226).
- Fix `calculate_breakdown_pay` overpaying overnight breakdown stipends by one cent:
  the stipend is $85.00 per midnight crossed (was $85.01), so a breakdown reported at
  22:00 on 2026-04-02 and repaired at 03:00 on 2026-04-03 now pays $139.00 instead of
  $139.01. Same-day breakdown pay is unchanged (CT-227).
- Fix `calculate_inside_delivery_fee` omitting the threshold heavy-handling bump at
  exactly 25 pieces: the bump was only applied above 25 pieces, so a threshold stop
  with 1 floor, no elevator and 25 pieces priced at $115.00 instead of $125.50.
  Threshold stops now get the bump at 25 or more pieces as documented, while
  non-threshold services and counts below 25 keep their current pricing (CT-223).
- Fix `build_invoice` reporting a subtotal that does not tie out to the printed
  lines: the subtotal is now the sum of the rounded line amounts instead of a
  re-rounding of the unrounded extended charges, so INV-204417 prints lines of
  $2,989.27, $545.82 and $125.03 with a subtotal and total of $3,660.12 rather
  than $3,660.11. Invoices whose line rounding already tied out are unchanged
  (CT-222).
- Fix `calculate_trailer_inspection_due` raising `TypeError` for a failed last
  inspection: the reinspection reason suffix was built with string subtraction
  instead of concatenation, so failed-inspection trailers got no due date or
  odometer limit at all. A trailer inspected at 70,000 miles, now at 70,499
  miles on day 6 with a failed result now returns day 7 / 70,500 miles with
  reason `standard+reinspect` (CT-220).
- Fix `find_excursions` dropping a 30-minute reefer excursion whose first
  in-range reading is also the reading that closes it: the excursion now ends at
  the first reading back inside the range (as documented) rather than the last
  out-of-range reading, so TW-91033 (setpoint 34F +/- 4, 39F or warmer 22:05
  through 22:30, 37F at 22:35) is reported as a 30-minute excursion instead of
  nothing (CT-221).
- Fix `find_conflicts` in `dock_schedule` missing overlaps behind a long unload:
  each appointment is now checked against every earlier appointment still holding
  the door, not just the immediate predecessor, so a floor-load unload booked
  08:00-12:00 reports conflicts with later appointments at 09:00 and 10:00
  instead of only the first one (CT-219).
- Fix `calculate_edi_997_ack_status` accepting a materially incomplete 997
  interchange: the overage rate was forced to zero whenever included transactions
  exceeded accepted plus rejected, so any shortfall passed tolerance. A 997 with
  9,950 accepted of 10,000 included (0.50% overage, matching control numbers) now
  returns `COUNT_MISMATCH` under the 0.20% default overage tolerance, while
  within-tolerance overage and exact counts still return `ACCEPTED` (CT-218).
- Fix `parse_bol_references` lifting an all-zero payload to `1`: a reference such
  as `PU-0` now stays `ParsedReference("PU", "0")` instead of becoming
  `ParsedReference("PU", "1")`, so valid pickup numbers are no longer shifted to
  a different identifier (CT-216).

- Fix `fuel_surcharge_for_shipment` billing Fri-Sun pickups at the following
  Monday's DOE price: the surcharge now uses the most recent price published on
  or before the pickup date, so TW-90266 (Friday 2026-09-18, 1,000 mi) bills
  $470.00 at the 9/14 price of $4.03 instead of $430.00 at 9/21's $3.79 (CT-217).
- Fix `map_edi_210_charges` mapping unknown nonblank EDI 210 charge codes to
  `misc` instead of the generic `other` bucket: an unknown code such as `ABC`
  now maps to `other` with source `fallback`. Blank codes still use the
  amount-threshold fallback, and `999` keeps its existing `other` mapping
  (CT-215).
- Fix `calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement` overcounting remaining quarterly
  selections: the year is now treated as four quarters instead of three, so a
  40-driver pool at a 25% annual rate with 4 prior selections returns 3 for the
  current quarter rather than 6 (CT-213).
- Fix `calculate_mode_conversion_factor` inflating LTL-to-truckload conversions by

- Fix `calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement` rejecting `period_number` 12 for

# Changelog

All notable changes to carrier-utils.

## Unreleased

- Fix `map_edi_210_charges` treating zero-dollar EDI 210 lines as real charges:
  the ignore check covered only one-cent lines, so a zero-amount `DET` detention
  line was categorized as detention from its code and added invoice-review noise.
  Zero-dollar lines now return category `ignore` with amount `0.00` and source
  `amount`, while non-zero lines (including non-zero `DET`) keep their existing
  categorization and source (CT-235).
- Fix `calculate_team_driver_premium` subtracting a contract's flat addition
  instead of adding it: the flat add-on is now applied on top of the
  multiplier-adjusted premium, so a 300-mile team request under a 1.10x contract
  with a $20.00 flat addition returns $79.40 instead of $39.40. Contracts with
  no flat addition price unchanged (CT-234).
- Fix `allocate_toll_costs` raising a validation error on zero-toll and zero-mile
  segments: zero values are now treated as non-billable and skipped rather than
  rejected (negative values are still invalid), so a trip with a waived $5.00 toll
  over 12 miles, a $0.00 toll over 12 miles and an $8.00 toll over 0.00 miles
  allocates $0.00 to customer, driver and carrier instead of failing before
  settlement. Shipments with only billable segments allocate unchanged (CT-232).
- Fix `find_excursions` carrying a reefer excursion across a logger gap: the
  logger-gap split compared each reading against itself instead of the previous
  reading, so a gap never ended the run and the excursion looked closed and
  longer than observed. An out-of-range run now ends at the last reading before
  a gap longer than 15 minutes and is reported as open, so the reported case
  (readings every 5 minutes 22:00-22:30, then nothing until 23:10 at 34F) is a
  30.0-minute open excursion ending 22:30 instead of a closed 70.0-minute one.
  Excursions over continuous readings are unchanged (CT-233).
- Fix `calculate_mode_conversion_factor` applying the hazmat uplift to drayage
  conversions as a subtraction instead of an addition: a hazmat truckload-to-drayage
  move of 12,000 lb over 200 miles with 2 stops now returns 0.7700 (0.7600 base plus
  the 0.0100 drayage hazmat uplift) instead of 0.7500, correcting every hazmat
  drayage quote and settlement tied to this factor. Non-hazmat conversions and
  hazmat conversions to other target modes are unchanged (CT-231).
- Fix `calculate_washout_fee` applying the hazmat washout premium even when the
  contract disallows it: the pass-through maximum is now the standard rate when
  `allow_hazmat_premium` is false, so a hazmat load with a $220.00 receipt
  reimburses $70.00 instead of $205.00. Contracts that allow the premium keep
  the full hazmat maximum and settle unchanged (CT-230).

- Fix `calculate_driver_medical_due` keeping drivers in grace past the documented
  15-day post-expiration window: `GRACE_DAYS` is now 15 instead of 16, so a record
  that expired 16 days ago returns status `expired` with no grace end date, and a
  record that expired 3 days ago returns a grace end date of 2026-04-13 instead of
  2026-04-14. Records still within grace keep returning `grace` and remain
  dispatch-ineligible (CT-228).
- Fix `parse_rate_confirmation` reading trailing note numbers as the amount: a
  dollar amount now wins over numbers in a note that follows it, so Hartline
  multi-stop rate con TW-88412 parses `Stop Off: $100.00 (1 extra stop)` as
  $100.00 (not $1.00) and `Detention: $75.00/hr after 2 hrs free` as $75.00 (not
  $2.00), letting the flat charges tie out to the $2,847.50 total. Rate cons
  without trailing notes parse unchanged (CT-229).

- Fix `calculate_short_pay_variance` understating the early-pay discount by
  subtracting fuel from the discount base instead of adding it: the discount is
  now a percent of the full pre-tax subtotal (linehaul + fuel + accessorial +
  other, tax excluded), so an invoice of $1,155.00 (linehaul $1,000.00, fuel
  $100.00, tax $55.00) with a $1,133.00 payment on the due date shows an
  expected amount of $1,133.00 and no short pay instead of a $4.00 short pay
  (CT-225).

- Fix `calculate_trailer_inspection_due` marking hazmat trailers due a day early:
  the hazmat calendar limit is now the documented 45 days instead of 44, so a
  California hazmat trailer last inspected on day 0 at 40,000 miles and read on
  day 44 at 47,000 miles is due February 15, 2026 with reason `hazmat` rather
  than February 14, 2026. Non-hazmat and other-jurisdiction schedules are
  unchanged (CT-226).
- Fix `calculate_breakdown_pay` overpaying overnight breakdown stipends by one cent:
  the stipend is $85.00 per midnight crossed (was $85.01), so a breakdown reported at
  22:00 on 2026-04-02 and repaired at 03:00 on 2026-04-03 now pays $139.00 instead of
  $139.01. Same-day breakdown pay is unchanged (CT-227).
- Fix `calculate_inside_delivery_fee` omitting the threshold heavy-handling bump at
  exactly 25 pieces: the bump was only applied above 25 pieces, so a threshold stop
  with 1 floor, no elevator and 25 pieces priced at $115.00 instead of $125.50.
  Threshold stops now get the bump at 25 or more pieces as documented, while
  non-threshold services and counts below 25 keep their current pricing (CT-223).
- Fix `build_invoice` reporting a subtotal that does not tie out to the printed
  lines: the subtotal is now the sum of the rounded line amounts instead of a
  re-rounding of the unrounded extended charges, so INV-204417 prints lines of
  $2,989.27, $545.82 and $125.03 with a subtotal and total of $3,660.12 rather
  than $3,660.11. Invoices whose line rounding already tied out are unchanged
  (CT-222).
- Fix `calculate_trailer_inspection_due` raising `TypeError` for a failed last
  inspection: the reinspection reason suffix was built with string subtraction
  instead of concatenation, so failed-inspection trailers got no due date or
  odometer limit at all. A trailer inspected at 70,000 miles, now at 70,499
  miles on day 6 with a failed result now returns day 7 / 70,500 miles with
  reason `standard+reinspect` (CT-220).
- Fix `find_excursions` dropping a 30-minute reefer excursion whose first
  in-range reading is also the reading that closes it: the excursion now ends at
  the first reading back inside the range (as documented) rather than the last
  out-of-range reading, so TW-91033 (setpoint 34F +/- 4, 39F or warmer 22:05
  through 22:30, 37F at 22:35) is reported as a 30-minute excursion instead of
  nothing (CT-221).
- Fix `find_conflicts` in `dock_schedule` missing overlaps behind a long unload:
  each appointment is now checked against every earlier appointment still holding
  the door, not just the immediate predecessor, so a floor-load unload booked
  08:00-12:00 reports conflicts with later appointments at 09:00 and 10:00
  instead of only the first one (CT-219).
- Fix `calculate_edi_997_ack_status` accepting a materially incomplete 997
  interchange: the overage rate was forced to zero whenever included transactions
  exceeded accepted plus rejected, so any shortfall passed tolerance. A 997 with
  9,950 accepted of 10,000 included (0.50% overage, matching control numbers) now
  returns `COUNT_MISMATCH` under the 0.20% default overage tolerance, while
  within-tolerance overage and exact counts still return `ACCEPTED` (CT-218).
- Fix `parse_bol_references` lifting an all-zero payload to `1`: a reference such
  as `PU-0` now stays `ParsedReference("PU", "0")` instead of becoming
  `ParsedReference("PU", "1")`, so valid pickup numbers are no longer shifted to
  a different identifier (CT-216).

- Fix `fuel_surcharge_for_shipment` billing Fri-Sun pickups at the following
  Monday's DOE price: the surcharge now uses the most recent price published on
  or before the pickup date, so TW-90266 (Friday 2026-09-18, 1,000 mi) bills
  $470.00 at the 9/14 price of $4.03 instead of $430.00 at 9/21's $3.79 (CT-217).
- Fix `map_edi_210_charges` mapping unknown nonblank EDI 210 charge codes to
  `misc` instead of the generic `other` bucket: an unknown code such as `ABC`
  now maps to `other` with source `fallback`. Blank codes still use the
  amount-threshold fallback, and `999` keeps its existing `other` mapping
  (CT-215).
- Fix `calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement` overcounting remaining quarterly
  selections: the year is now treated as four quarters instead of three, so a
  40-driver pool at a 25% annual rate with 4 prior selections returns 3 for the
  current quarter rather than 6 (CT-213).
- Fix `calculate_mode_conversion_factor` inflating LTL-to-truckload conversions by

from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from road_use_tax import JurisdictionMiles, TaxTerms, calculate_road_use_tax


def test_loaded_and_empty_miles_are_taxed():
    miles = JurisdictionMiles(name="OR", loaded_miles=Decimal("120"), empty_miles=Decimal("30"))
    terms = TaxTerms(rate_per_mile=Decimal("0.08"))
    assert calculate_road_use_tax(miles, terms) == Decimal("12.00")


def test_yard_and_ferry_miles_do_not_count():
    miles = JurisdictionMiles(
        name="KY",
        loaded_miles=Decimal("50"),
        empty_miles=Decimal("20"),
        yard_miles=Decimal("200"),
        ferry_miles=Decimal("40"),
    )
    terms = TaxTerms(rate_per_mile=Decimal("0.10"))
    assert calculate_road_use_tax(miles, terms) == Decimal("7.00")


def test_exempt_miles_reduce_taxable_miles():
    miles = JurisdictionMiles(
        name="NM",
        loaded_miles=Decimal("100"),
        empty_miles=Decimal("20"),
        exempt_miles=Decimal("25"),
    )
    terms = TaxTerms(rate_per_mile=Decimal("0.12"))
    assert calculate_road_use_tax(miles, terms) == Decimal("11.40")


def test_fewer_than_ten_taxable_miles_is_de_minimis():
    miles = JurisdictionMiles(name="NY", loaded_miles=Decimal("9.99"))
    terms = TaxTerms(rate_per_mile=Decimal("0.50"))
    assert calculate_road_use_tax(miles, terms) == Decimal("0.00")


def test_exactly_ten_taxable_miles_is_taxed():
    miles = JurisdictionMiles(name="NY", loaded_miles=Decimal("10.00"))
    terms = TaxTerms(rate_per_mile=Decimal("0.50"))
    assert calculate_road_use_tax(miles, terms) == Decimal("5.00")


def test_half_up_rounding_applies_to_base_tax():
    miles = JurisdictionMiles(name="UT", loaded_miles=Decimal("3"), empty_miles=Decimal("7"))
    terms = TaxTerms(rate_per_mile=Decimal("0.3335"))

def test_electric_surcharge_applies_at_threshold():

# Changelog

All notable changes to carrier-utils.

## Unreleased

- Fix `calculate_inside_delivery_fee` billing the threshold minimum one cent high:
  the default minimum charge is now $55.00 (was $55.01), so a threshold stop with
  1 floor, no elevator and 1 piece returns $55.00 instead of $55.01. Stops whose
  computed amount already exceeds the minimum keep their current pricing (CT-237).
- Fix `calculate_washout_fee` reimbursing dry freight that requires no wash:
  the no-wash level returned one cent instead of zero, so a dry load with
  required wash level `none` and a $22.00 receipt reimbursed $0.01. The no-wash
  level now reimburses $0.00, while washouts that require a wash settle
  unchanged (CT-236).
- Fix `map_edi_210_charges` treating zero-dollar EDI 210 lines as real charges:
  the ignore check covered only one-cent lines, so a zero-amount `DET` detention
  line was categorized as detention from its code and added invoice-review noise.
  Zero-dollar lines now return category `ignore` with amount `0.00` and source
  `amount`, while non-zero lines (including non-zero `DET`) keep their existing
  categorization and source (CT-235).
- Fix `calculate_team_driver_premium` subtracting a contract's flat addition
  instead of adding it: the flat add-on is now applied on top of the
  multiplier-adjusted premium, so a 300-mile team request under a 1.10x contract
  with a $20.00 flat addition returns $79.40 instead of $39.40. Contracts with
  no flat addition price unchanged (CT-234).
- Fix `allocate_toll_costs` raising a validation error on zero-toll and zero-mile
  segments: zero values are now treated as non-billable and skipped rather than
  rejected (negative values are still invalid), so a trip with a waived $5.00 toll
  over 12 miles, a $0.00 toll over 12 miles and an $8.00 toll over 0.00 miles
  allocates $0.00 to customer, driver and carrier instead of failing before
  settlement. Shipments with only billable segments allocate unchanged (CT-232).
- Fix `find_excursions` carrying a reefer excursion across a logger gap: the
  logger-gap split compared each reading against itself instead of the previous
  reading, so a gap never ended the run and the excursion looked closed and
  longer than observed. An out-of-range run now ends at the last reading before
  a gap longer than 15 minutes and is reported as open, so the reported case
  (readings every 5 minutes 22:00-22:30, then nothing until 23:10 at 34F) is a
  30.0-minute open excursion ending 22:30 instead of a closed 70.0-minute one.
  Excursions over continuous readings are unchanged (CT-233).
- Fix `calculate_mode_conversion_factor` applying the hazmat uplift to drayage
  conversions as a subtraction instead of an addition: a hazmat truckload-to-drayage
  move of 12,000 lb over 200 miles with 2 stops now returns 0.7700 (0.7600 base plus
  the 0.0100 drayage hazmat uplift) instead of 0.7500, correcting every hazmat
  drayage quote and settlement tied to this factor. Non-hazmat conversions and
  hazmat conversions to other target modes are unchanged (CT-231).
- Fix `calculate_washout_fee` applying the hazmat washout premium even when the
  contract disallows it: the pass-through maximum is now the standard rate when
  `allow_hazmat_premium` is false, so a hazmat load with a $220.00 receipt
  reimburses $70.00 instead of $205.00. Contracts that allow the premium keep
  the full hazmat maximum and settle unchanged (CT-230).

- Fix `calculate_driver_medical_due` keeping drivers in grace past the documented
  15-day post-expiration window: `GRACE_DAYS` is now 15 instead of 16, so a record
  that expired 16 days ago returns status `expired` with no grace end date, and a
  record that expired 3 days ago returns a grace end date of 2026-04-13 instead of
  2026-04-14. Records still within grace keep returning `grace` and remain
  dispatch-ineligible (CT-228).
- Fix `parse_rate_confirmation` reading trailing note numbers as the amount: a
  dollar amount now wins over numbers in a note that follows it, so Hartline
  multi-stop rate con TW-88412 parses `Stop Off: $100.00 (1 extra stop)` as
  $100.00 (not $1.00) and `Detention: $75.00/hr after 2 hrs free` as $75.00 (not
  $2.00), letting the flat charges tie out to the $2,847.50 total. Rate cons
  without trailing notes parse unchanged (CT-229).

- Fix `calculate_short_pay_variance` understating the early-pay discount by
  subtracting fuel from the discount base instead of adding it: the discount is
  now a percent of the full pre-tax subtotal (linehaul + fuel + accessorial +
  other, tax excluded), so an invoice of $1,155.00 (linehaul $1,000.00, fuel
  $100.00, tax $55.00) with a $1,133.00 payment on the due date shows an
  expected amount of $1,133.00 and no short pay instead of a $4.00 short pay
  (CT-225).

- Fix `calculate_trailer_inspection_due` marking hazmat trailers due a day early:
  the hazmat calendar limit is now the documented 45 days instead of 44, so a
  California hazmat trailer last inspected on day 0 at 40,000 miles and read on
  day 44 at 47,000 miles is due February 15, 2026 with reason `hazmat` rather
  than February 14, 2026. Non-hazmat and other-jurisdiction schedules are
  unchanged (CT-226).
- Fix `calculate_breakdown_pay` overpaying overnight breakdown stipends by one cent:
  the stipend is $85.00 per midnight crossed (was $85.01), so a breakdown reported at
  22:00 on 2026-04-02 and repaired at 03:00 on 2026-04-03 now pays $139.00 instead of
  $139.01. Same-day breakdown pay is unchanged (CT-227).
- Fix `calculate_inside_delivery_fee` omitting the threshold heavy-handling bump at
  exactly 25 pieces: the bump was only applied above 25 pieces, so a threshold stop
  with 1 floor, no elevator and 25 pieces priced at $115.00 instead of $125.50.
  Threshold stops now get the bump at 25 or more pieces as documented, while
  non-threshold services and counts below 25 keep their current pricing (CT-223).
- Fix `build_invoice` reporting a subtotal that does not tie out to the printed
  lines: the subtotal is now the sum of the rounded line amounts instead of a
  re-rounding of the unrounded extended charges, so INV-204417 prints lines of
  $2,989.27, $545.82 and $125.03 with a subtotal and total of $3,660.12 rather
  than $3,660.11. Invoices whose line rounding already tied out are unchanged
  (CT-222).
- Fix `calculate_trailer_inspection_due` raising `TypeError` for a failed last
  inspection: the reinspection reason suffix was built with string subtraction
  instead of concatenation, so failed-inspection trailers got no due date or
  odometer limit at all. A trailer inspected at 70,000 miles, now at 70,499
  miles on day 6 with a failed result now returns day 7 / 70,500 miles with
  reason `standard+reinspect` (CT-220).
- Fix `find_excursions` dropping a 30-minute reefer excursion whose first
  in-range reading is also the reading that closes it: the excursion now ends at
  the first reading back inside the range (as documented) rather than the last
  out-of-range reading, so TW-91033 (setpoint 34F +/- 4, 39F or warmer 22:05
  through 22:30, 37F at 22:35) is reported as a 30-minute excursion instead of
  nothing (CT-221).
- Fix `find_conflicts` in `dock_schedule` missing overlaps behind a long unload:
  each appointment is now checked against every earlier appointment still holding
  the door, not just the immediate predecessor, so a floor-load unload booked
  08:00-12:00 reports conflicts with later appointments at 09:00 and 10:00
  instead of only the first one (CT-219).
- Fix `calculate_edi_997_ack_status` accepting a materially incomplete 997
  interchange: the overage rate was forced to zero whenever included transactions
  exceeded accepted plus rejected, so any shortfall passed tolerance. A 997 with
  9,950 accepted of 10,000 included (0.50% overage, matching control numbers) now
  returns `COUNT_MISMATCH` under the 0.20% default overage tolerance, while
  within-tolerance overage and exact counts still return `ACCEPTED` (CT-218).
- Fix `parse_bol_references` lifting an all-zero payload to `1`: a reference such
  as `PU-0` now stays `ParsedReference("PU", "0")` instead of becoming
  `ParsedReference("PU", "1")`, so valid pickup numbers are no longer shifted to
  a different identifier (CT-216).

- Fix `fuel_surcharge_for_shipment` billing Fri-Sun pickups at the following
  Monday's DOE price: the surcharge now uses the most recent price published on
  or before the pickup date, so TW-90266 (Friday 2026-09-18, 1,000 mi) bills
  $470.00 at the 9/14 price of $4.03 instead of $430.00 at 9/21's $3.79 (CT-217).
- Fix `map_edi_210_charges` mapping unknown nonblank EDI 210 charge codes to
  `misc` instead of the generic `other` bucket: an unknown code such as `ABC`
  now maps to `other` with source `fallback`. Blank codes still use the
  amount-threshold fallback, and `999` keeps its existing `other` mapping
  (CT-215).
- Fix `calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement` overcounting remaining quarterly
  selections: the year is now treated as four quarters instead of three, so a
  40-driver pool at a 25% annual rate with 4 prior selections returns 3 for the
  current quarter rather than 6 (CT-213).
- Fix `calculate_mode_conversion_factor` inflating LTL-to-truckload conversions by
  a basis point: the LTL-to-truckload base factor is corrected to 0.8500 (was
  0.8501), so a 10,000 lb move over 1,000 miles with 2 stops now returns 0.8200
  instead of 0.8201 (CT-214).

- Fix `calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement` rejecting `period_number` 12 for
  monthly programs: December is now a valid final period, so the requirement is
  calculated (and capped at the eligible population) instead of raising
  `ValueError` (CT-212).
- Fix `allocate_fuel_purchases` raising on eligible zero-mile trips: a
  zero-odometer-change trip is now valid and the purchase is allocated to the
  first eligible trip instead of failing before settlement (CT-211).

- Fix `tender_expires_at` expiring Friday-evening tenders on Saturday 09:00
  instead of the next business morning: the next-business-day rollover no
  longer stops on Saturday (or skips to Tuesday from a weekend), so a Friday
  18:00 tender now expires Monday 09:00 (CT-210).
- Fix `lookup_lane_rate` falling straight to the customer default when the most
  specific lane rate on file has expired: an expired lane now falls back to the
  next less specific level (for example Hartline's OR to ID state rate) instead
  of the default per-mile rate (CT-209).
- Fix `ifta_return` dropping jurisdictions with tax-paid fuel but no miles
  driven: a fuel-only member jurisdiction now gets a line with zero taxable
  gallons so its tax-paid gallons come back as a credit (CT-208).
- Fix `calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement` rejecting a valid zero annual
  rate: `annual_rate=0` now returns zero selections instead of raising
  `ValueError`, while negative rates are still rejected (CT-206).
- Fix false 30-minute break violations in `break_violations`: consecutive
  non-driving segments (for example an on-duty fuel stop followed by an
  off-duty meal) now add up toward the break (CT-205).
- Fix `estimate_arrival` producing ETAs that are too early for drivers who
  spent on-duty time loading before departure: the 30-minute break now counts
  against the remaining 14-hour window, so a run that cannot finish in the
  window schedules the required 10-hour reset (CT-204).
- Fix `check_axle_weights` missing bridge-formula violations on interior axle
  groups: every group of two or more consecutive axles is now checked, not just
  the outer bridge (CT-203).
- Fix long-haul discount being added instead of subtracted at 1,000+ paid miles
  in `calculate_linehaul_rate_per_mile` (CT-202).
- Fix multi-line LTL quotes overstating linear feet: lines with the same pallet
  footprint now share rows in `linear_feet_for_shipment`.
